written.myAnswer: A tissue is a group of similar cells working together to perform specific functions. An organ is made of different related tissues working together to perform specific functions.

Atoms combine to form molecules; molecules make up organelles; organelles work together within cells; similar cells form tissues; tissues form organs; organs work together in organ systems; and organ systems together make an organism. Each level builds on the previous one, enabling increasingly complex functions that support the organism.

A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform specific functions. Plant tissues are broadly classified as meristematic tissues, which divide and enable growth, and permanent tissues, which perform functions such as protection, support, and transport. Animal tissues include epithelial tissue (covering and lining), connective tissue (supporting and binding), muscular tissue (movement), and nervous tissue (conducting signals).

Organ systems work in coordination to maintain the organism’s vital functions. If one system fails, it can disrupt the functions of other systems that depend on it, and the organism may not function normally.
